message.content:
Fusion research has long driven advances beyond power generation, benefiting society in practical ways.
Superconducting magnets developed for tokamaks improved MRI systems, enabling clearer medical imaging and smaller devices.
Plasma diagnostics and vacuum technology helped semiconductor manufacturing create thinner, more reliable electronic chips.
High-temperature materials and remote maintenance tools from fusion projects support safer nuclear waste handling and industrial robotics.
Even iritic modeling of particle beams has sharpened accelerator methods used in cancer proton therapy.
These spillover innovations show that fusion research strengthens medicine, manufacturing, energy safety, and scientific training.
